articles.content: Kilo Console (Beta) is live! - by Arkadiy Kondrashov Kilo Blog Subscribe Sign in Kilo Console (Beta) is live! Manage git worktrees, sessions and settings with browser-based UI. Arkadiy Kondrashov Jun 11, 2026 11 15 Share Kilo Console is a local, browser-based UI for the Kilo CLI . It gives you one place to manage your projects, git worktrees, sessions, and settings — without hand-editing JSON config files. This guide walks through the basics. Kilo Console is in beta. Watch video for a quick overview or read the walkthrough below. Thanks for reading Kilo Blog! Subscribe for free to receive new posts and support my work. Subscribe Open the console Start it from your terminal. You will need to install a Release Candidate package since it’s still an experimental feature: npm -g install @kiloco

articles.content: You Don't Have to Use Fable and Mythos to Work on the Frontier Kilo Blog Subscribe Sign in You Don't Have to Use Fable and Mythos to Work on the Frontier In a complex regulatory environment, model freedom ensures that your workflows don't stop Ari Messer Jun 15, 2026 6 3 1 Share When Anthropic dropped Claude Fable 5 and Mythos 5 last week, the reaction was immediate. Fable 5 scored 80.3% on SWE-bench Pro and an astonishing 85% on OS-World Verified for computer use, placing it state-of-the-art across nearly every benchmark. Mythos — the same underlying model with safeguards lifted — was even more remarkable, the kind of unconstrained research capability that explains why Anthropic had been restricting access under Project Glasswing for two months before public launch. tweets.creator: @spencerpratt
tweets.text: When you think of the most lovely and cherished buildings in LA...places you *want* to go, they're all Art Deco. We can make buildings look any way we want...why not choose this magical legacy and build like we care? Reject communism. Reject ugly. Embrace beauty.

tweets.creator: @spencerpratt
tweets.text: In music, it's often said D major is the key that resonates with the human soul. Schubart said it's "the key of triumph, of Hallejuahs, of war-cries, of victory-rejoicing." The "D major" of architecture is (D)eco. Art Deco is the defining aesthetic of the City of Angels.

tweets.creator: @spencerpratt
tweets.text: Predictably, this monstrosity remains largely empty; nobody wants to be here. This affront to beauty has become insta-blight, more likely to house Superman's arch-nemesis than any functional business. The communist's worship of ugliness has profound impacts on society.

tweets.creator: @spencerpratt
tweets.text: Conversely, commie slopitecture repels us. This ugliness poisons the soul. You want to avert your eyes from this stain on our skyline. How can you enjoy or take pride in where you live if you don't even want to look at it? It looks like the wreckage of some great tragedy.

tweets.creator: @spencerpratt
tweets.text: The City had a 150' height limit, but ECB's trademark clock tower was granted an exemption, because beauty should always supersede bureaucracy. Breathtaking architecture like this is a magnet...it draws us in, makes us *want* to be here, and inspires us to do great things here.

tweets.creator: @spencerpratt
tweets.text: The Eastern Columbia Building is the benchmark for art deco beauty in LA. Built a century ago, during the throes of the Depression in just *9 months*; a testament to what Angelenos are capable of, in any adverse circumstances, when they actually give a damn.

tweets.creator: @spencerpratt
tweets.text: One of the hallmarks of communism is the exaltation of ugliness. Contrast our gorgeous Depression-era LA architecture with the commie brutalist slop vomited upon us today. I'll support any candidate who vows to throw this architect in prison for crimes against beauty.
